title: The Hubble radius, the cosmic horizon, and the Schwarzschild radius are not the same concept
text: First distinguish the scales: the Hubble radius is R_H=c/H(t); in a spatially flat FLRW universe, substituting the critical density ρ_c=3H²/(8πG) into the mass-energy inside the Hubble sphere M=(4π/3)ρ_cR_H³ yields 2GM/c²=R_H. This equality comes from the Friedmann equations; it is not two numbers that happen to be equal today, and it does not prove that the universe is a Schwarzschild black hole. The Schwarzschild solution describes a static, spherically symmetric, externally vacuum, asymptotically flat spacetime; FLRW describes a dynamic, approximately homogeneous and isotropic universe. The Hubble radius, the cosmological apparent horizon, the particle horizon, and the event horizon must be stated separately and cannot be lumped together as the radius of the observable universe.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. Kept as its own id beside astro-horizon; the two cards are the same modern horizon argument.

title: Black-hole universes and parent universes are a family of hypotheses, not an established conclusion
text: "Our universe was born inside a black hole in another universe" is not simply a synonym for the multiverse, but a family of concrete yet unconfirmed models. Different versions use patching of classical general relativity, black-hole interior cosmology, or, in Einstein-Cartan theory, torsion to replace the singularity with a bounce. The preceding-level universe that produced the black hole can be colloquially called the parent universe, but one must first ask the user which model they mean; existing research shows that it can be constructed mathematically, which does not mean observations have proven that our universe actually originated this way.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. Parent-universe and black-hole cosmology, including arXiv:2007.11556 and arXiv:1106.4427, are later hypotheses.

title: Mass and weight
text: Mass is the inertia, and the source of gravity. Weight is the force, mg, in a particular gravitational field. The same mass weighs less on the Moon.

title: Work and energy
text: Work is force through a distance, a transfer. Energy is a state. For a conservative force the work equals the drop in potential energy; the two words are not synonyms.

title: Force and momentum
text: Force is the rate of change of momentum. F=ma is that statement only when the mass stays constant.

title: Torque and energy
text: Torque is r cross F, and it depends on which point you measure from. Energy does not. A newton-metre of torque is not a joule of work until something actually turns.

title: Inertial mass and gravitational mass
text: The mass in F=ma and the mass in Newton's law of gravity are defined by different experiments. That they agree is a fact, the one the equivalence principle takes seriously.

title: Centrifugal force and centripetal force
text: In an inertial frame the force on a thing moving in a circle points toward the center. Centrifugal force shows up only when you insist on standing in the rotating frame.

title: Temperature and heat
text: Temperature is a state. Heat is energy crossing the boundary because of a temperature difference. A hot object does not 'contain heat' in the way it contains energy.

title: Heat and internal energy
text: Internal energy is a state of the system. Heat and work are ways energy crosses the boundary. An object does not contain a stock of heat.

title: Entropy and 'disorder'
text: Entropy counts microscopic arrangements, k ln W. Calling it disorder is a metaphor, and two unlike messes can share one entropy.

title: Temperature and average molecular kinetic energy
text: For a monatomic ideal gas the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT. A gas that can rotate or vibrate has more places to put the energy, so that formula is not universal.

title: Carnot efficiency and real efficiency
text: One minus the cold temperature over the hot temperature is the ceiling for a reversible engine. A real engine is lower. The formula does not tell you the power.

title: Charge and current
text: Charge is a stock, in coulombs. Current is how fast that stock passes a point, in amperes. They are not two names for one quantity.

title: Electric field and electric potential
text: The electric field is a vector. The potential is a scalar. E is minus the gradient of V, so the field can be nonzero in direction while you move on a surface of constant V only if you leave that surface.

title: B and H
text: In the magnetism lectures, B is the magnetic flux density, including how the material answers, and H is the field tied to the free currents. In vacuum, B = mu0 H. In a ferromagnet they are not the same quantity. Treating them as one number is the usual mistake.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume II, magnetic materials
support.note: B includes the material's answer. H is tied to the free currents. In vacuum, B = mu0 H.

title: Resistance and resistivity
text: Resistance belongs to a piece of material of a certain shape. Resistivity belongs to the stuff. The same copper drawn differently has a different resistance.

title: Phase velocity and group velocity
text: Phase velocity is ω/k, the speed of a crest. Group velocity is dω/dk, the speed of the lump of energy. In a dispersive medium they differ, and a phase speed faster than light does not carry a message.

title: Frequency and wavelength
text: The source sets the frequency. When a wave enters a new medium the frequency stays and the wavelength changes with the speed.

title: Amplitude and intensity
text: Intensity goes as the square of the amplitude. Double the amplitude and the intensity goes up by four, which is also how he treats the probability as the square of an arrow.

title: Interference and diffraction
text: Interference and diffraction are both the adding of waves. He said nobody has ever separated them by a real physical difference; the names are a custom.

title: The uncertainty principle and 'measurement disturbance'
text: The uncertainty principle is a property of the wave, a Fourier fact, not a story about a clumsy measurement bumping the particle.

title: Superposition and mixture
text: A superposition is one state, amplitudes added, with cross terms. A mixture is a probability of being in one state or another, and the cross terms are gone.

title: Entanglement and superluminal communication
text: Entanglement gives correlations, but the results of local measurements are each random; to see the correlations one must exchange classical information. The most easily confused step: claiming that entanglement allows messages to travel faster than light. When judging, first ask which layer it is—definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. No-signaling is standard quantum mechanics, but this wording is not a passage from his lectures, so it is not filed as his.

title: Spin and 'rotation'
text: Spin is angular momentum a particle has without being a little ball. If you force the electron to be a classical spinning sphere of the usual radius, the equator would have to move faster than light. That picture is the wrong one.

title: Virtual particles and real particles
text: A real particle can travel off to a detector. A virtual particle is an internal line, off the mass shell, a piece of the amplitude.

support.source: QED: The Strange Theory of Light and Matter

title: Time dilation and 'clocks running slow'
text: The time between two ticks of a clock is shortest in the clock's own frame. What you see with your eyes also mixes in light-travel delay and the Doppler shift. Those are not the same correction.

title: Rest mass and relativistic mass
text: In E² = (pc)² + (mc²)² the m is the rest mass, the same in every frame. Calling γm a relativistic mass mixes a frame-dependent factor into the mass.

title: Gravity and spacetime curvature
text: In the slow, weak limit, Newtonian gravity is enough. Locally, in free fall, that force is transformed away. What you can still measure nearby is the tide, the difference of the pull from one place to the next. Do not spend curvature language on a single local force and call the result a tide.

support.source: The Character of Physical Law, the lecture on gravitation; Lectures on Gravitation
support.note: Newtonian gravity is the slow, weak limit. What you still measure locally in free fall is the tide.

title: The Hubble radius, the cosmic horizon, and the Schwarzschild radius
text: R_H=c/H is a scale, the horizon is a causal structure; in FLRW, 2GM/c²=R_H comes from the Friedmann equations and does not prove that the universe is a black hole. The most easily confused step: lumping the three radii together as 'the radius of the observable universe.' When judging, first ask which layer it is—definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. Kept as its own id beside cosmo-horizon-001; the two cards are the same modern horizon argument.

title: Redshift and distance
text: Cosmological redshift comes from the scale factor 1+z=a0/a, not from the Doppler effect; converting to distance via Hubble's law requires stating which distance is used. The most easily confused step: using the Doppler formula to compute the velocity of a high-redshift object. When judging, first ask which layer it is—definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. The scale-factor formula for cosmological redshift, and which distance Hubble's law is using, is modern cosmology rather than a passage from his lectures.

title: Dark energy and dark matter
text: Dark matter clumps (it has gravity, no electromagnetism), dark energy is approximately uniform (negative pressure, drives acceleration); the two act in opposite ways. The most easily confused step: treating them as the same kind of 'invisible stuff.' When judging, first ask which layer it is—definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. Dark energy, and the split from dark matter, is later cosmology.

title: Characteristic time and mean time
text: An estimate, a length divided by a speed, is a characteristic time. A mean time is an average over a distribution you have to name. Do not hand someone the estimate and call it the mean.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, order-of-magnitude estimates
support.note: A length over a speed is a characteristic time. A mean requires a distribution.

title: Friction and Friction-Generated Heat
text: Friction is a force. The energy it turns into heat is that force times the distance of slipping. A large force with almost no slip does not make a large amount of heat. Do not read the heat off the size of the force alone.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 4, Conservation of Energy
support.note: The heat is the friction force times the distance of slipping, not the force alone.

title: Elastic vs. Plastic Deformation
text: While the stretch is small, the force is proportional to the stretch, and the piece comes back. Past that limit it does not return to the old shape, and F = kx is the wrong law. Do not keep the spring formula after the material has yielded.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 38, Elasticity
support.note: Hooke's law is the small-stretch regime. Past it the piece does not spring back.

title: Pressure vs. Force
text: Pressure is force per area. The same weight on a small area and a large one is a different pressure. A bigger pressure is not by itself a bigger force.

title: Kinetic vs. Potential Energy
text: Kinetic energy depends on the frame you measure speed in. Potential energy depends on where you put zero. What the laws use is the change, or the sum when the force is conservative.

title: Escape Velocity vs. Orbital Velocity
text: A circular orbit needs speed sqrt(GM/r). To leave and not come back takes sqrt(2) times that, not twice that.

title: Temperature vs. Pressure
text: The ideal-gas law ties pressure and temperature, but you can raise the pressure at constant temperature by squeezing the volume. A rise in pressure is not a rise in temperature.

title: Reversible vs. Real Processes
text: Reversible is the limit of infinitely slow and no wasted motion. A real process makes entropy. The reversible number is a ceiling, not the output of the machine in front of you.

title: Specific Heat vs. Latent Heat
text: Specific heat is the energy to raise the temperature. Latent heat is the energy to change phase while the temperature stays put. You cannot use mcΔT across a boil.

title: Free Energy vs. Internal Energy
text: At a fixed temperature the direction of a change is not settled by the internal energy U alone. The free energy F = U - TS falls for a spontaneous change at fixed temperature and volume. A drop in U is not enough to decide.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, the thermodynamics chapters
support.note: At fixed temperature the direction is the free energy, not U alone.

title: Electric Field Strength vs. Electric Field Energy Density
text: E is the electric field strength. The energy in the electric field per unit volume goes as E squared, one-half epsilon0 E squared, not as E itself. Field strength is not energy.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume II, Chapter 27, Field Energy and Field Momentum
support.note: The electric energy per unit volume goes as E squared, not as E.

title: Capacitor vs. Battery
text: A capacitor stores charge, Q = CV, and the energy sits in the field. As it discharges, the voltage falls. A battery is a chemical cell that works to hold a potential. A discharging capacitor is not a constant-voltage source.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume II, electrostatics: capacitors and energy in the field
support.note: Q = CV, and the voltage of a discharging capacitor falls. A battery is a chemical cell.

title: Motional EMF vs. Induced EMF
text: Move a wire through a magnetic field and the force on the charges in the wire is the motional emf. Change the magnetic field through a loop that sits still and Faraday's law still gives an emf. One formula, two situations.

title: Dielectric vs. Conductor
text: In a conductor, free charges move until the electric field inside is zero. A dielectric only shifts its bound charges a little, and the field inside is not zero.

title: Resonance vs. Beats
text: Resonance is a drive near the natural frequency, so the amplitude grows. Beats are two nearby frequencies added, so the loudness pulses at the difference. They are not the same thing.

title: Refraction vs. Dispersion
text: Refraction is the bend at a surface because the speed changed. Dispersion is the speed depending on frequency, so different colors bend by different amounts.

title: Linear Superposition vs. Nonlinear Effects
text: When the wave equation is linear, two waves pass through each other and the displacements add. When the amplitude is large enough that the equation is no longer linear, the waves mix and new frequencies appear. Do not use superposition in that case.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, linear systems and waves
support.note: Superposition is the linear equation. Large amplitude can leave that equation.

title: Polarization vs. Intensity
text: Polarization is the direction of the oscillation. Intensity is the power flowing. Through a polarizer the transmitted intensity goes as the square of the cosine of the angle. A polarizer is not a plain knob for brightness.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, Chapter 33, Polarization
support.note: Polarization is the direction of the oscillation. The transmitted intensity goes as the square of the cosine.

title: Measurement vs. Wavefunction Collapse
text: The Schrödinger equation does not contain a collapse. Collapse is an extra instruction about what you write down when a measurement has distinguished outcomes. Decoherence is why the interference becomes impossible to see.

title: Tunneling vs. Passing Through a Wall
text: The chance of getting through a barrier falls exponentially as the barrier gets thicker. Tunneling is not a license for anything to walk through a wall, and it is not a violation of energy conservation.

title: Pauli Exclusion vs. Electron Shells
text: The Pauli principle is why electrons do not all sit in the lowest state, and why there are shells. The electrical attraction is what holds them to the nucleus. The shells are not the Coulomb force by itself.

title: Relativity of Simultaneity vs. Time Dilation
text: Two events that are simultaneous in one inertial frame need not be simultaneous in another. Time dilation is the comparison of a moving clock with the time between those events. They are one structure, not two unrelated effects.

title: Doppler Redshift vs. Cosmological Redshift
text: The former comes from relative velocity (including the transverse effect), the latter from the scale factor 1+z=a0/a; at high z the two differ numerically. The easiest step to conflate: using the Doppler formula to compute quasar distances. When judging, first ask which layer it is — definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. The high-redshift split between a Doppler shift and the scale-factor shift is a modern guardrail, not a passage from his lectures.

title: Special and General Relativistic Effects in GPS
text: Special relativity makes the satellite-borne clock run slow (about −7 microseconds per day), general relativity makes it run fast (about +45 microseconds per day), for a net of about +38 microseconds per day. The easiest step to conflate: saying only that relativity makes GPS run slow. When judging, first ask which layer it is — definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. The GPS clock budget, about -7 and +45 microseconds a day, net about +38, is modern engineering, not a number from his books.

title: Luminosity vs. Flux
text: What a source emits, its power, is not what one patch of a detector receives. If the light spreads over a sphere, the power per area falls as one over the square of the distance. Looking brighter is not the same as being a stronger source.

support.source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I, the inverse-square spreading of radiation
support.note: Power emitted is not power per area at the detector.

title: Black Hole Mass vs. Horizon Radius
text: The Schwarzschild radius is proportional to the mass, r = 2GM/c^2. A density estimated from the mass and that radius falls as the mass grows, because the volume grows faster than the mass. A large horizon is not, by that estimate, an extremely dense object.

support.source: Richard P. Feynman, Lectures on Gravitation
support.note: The Schwarzschild radius is proportional to the mass, so a density estimated from that radius falls as the mass grows.

title: Dark Matter vs. Modified Gravity
text: The former adds matter (invisible but still gravitating), the latter changes the equations; the criterion is which one can explain more observations at the same time. The easiest step to conflate: treating modified gravity as an answer that needs no dark matter. When judging, first ask which layer it is — definition, approximation, or observational effect.

support.note: Model-learned modern knowledge, not a passage from Feynman's corpus. Modified gravity set against particle dark matter is a later research split, not a lecture of his.

title: Order-of-Magnitude Estimation vs. Precise Calculation
text: An order-of-magnitude guess is for catching a crazy factor of ten. A precise calculation is for the percent. Neither one does the other's job.

support.source: FLP; Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!

title: Models vs. Real Systems
text: Every model has a list of things it leaves out: no friction, a point mass, an ideal gas. The conclusion holds inside that list. Taking the conclusion as a fact about the world, without the list, is the mistake.

support.source: Cargo Cult Science, 1974; The Feynman Lectures on Physics, which state the idealization before the law
support.note: The conclusion holds inside the list of things left out.

title: Correlation vs. Causation
text: Two things changing together are a correlation. That is not yet a cause. In the cargo-cult story the wooden airfield had the form of an airfield, and no airplanes came, because the form was not the cause. A cause needs the mechanism, or an intervention, not only the company of the two numbers.

support.note: The wooden airfield had the form and not the cause. Company of two numbers is not yet a mechanism.

title: Signal vs. Noise
text: One odd reading is not a discovery. You have to know the size of the scatter and how many readings you have. Two standard deviations and twenty standard deviations are not the same claim. Report the uncertainty, not only the striking point.

support.note: Report the uncertainty and the results that do not fit. One striking point is not a discovery.

title: Simulation Results vs. Experimental Verification
text: A computer run shows how this set of equations behaves, if the program is right. It does not show that the world behaves that way. That takes a measurement. Do not offer the run as the experiment.

support.source: Richard P. Feynman, Simulating Physics with Computers, International Journal of Theoretical Physics 21 (1982)
support.note: A run shows what the equations do, if the program is right. It is not the measurement.

title: Unit Conversion vs. Dimensional Analysis
text: Changing units changes the number. Dimensional analysis checks that both sides of an equation are the same kind of thing. A unit conversion will not catch a wrong power.

title: Which-Path Information and Measurement in the Double Slit
text: In the double slit the interference goes away when the experiment can tell which slit was used, not when a person decides to look. If the which-path record is only partial, the fringes fade rather than vanish. Single electrons still build the pattern one hit at a time.
